title: Matching the need to the option
objectives: Match seven client needs to suitable debt options, and name what to avoid.
Ask the two deciding questions: when is the money needed, and how would a 3% fall feel?
body_md:
Emergency fund or money needed any day: savings account, liquid or overnight fund — avoid long duration and credit risk funds. Money needed in 6–12 months: ultra short, low duration, money market fund or short FD — avoid long duration. Goal 1–3 years away: short duration, banking & PSU, corporate bond fund or target maturity fund matched to the date — avoid credit risk funds for essential goals. Goal 5+ years away wanting stability: target maturity, gilt or long duration (accepting rate swings), PPF — and don't treat debt as the whole plan; consider some equity too. Retiree needing regular income: SWP from a conservative debt fund, government small-savings schemes for eligible seniors, bond ladder — avoid high-yield bonds for essential income. Large long-term capital gain from property: 54EC bonds if eligible. Wants higher yield and understands the risk: a small slice in a credit risk fund or rated corporate bonds, diversified — never a large share in one issuer.

| Client need | Usually suitable | Avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Emergency fund, money needed any day | Savings account, liquid or overnight fund | Long duration, credit risk funds |
| Money needed in 6–12 months | Ultra short, low duration, money market fund; short FD | Long duration |
| Goal 1–3 years away | Short duration, banking & PSU, corporate bond fund; target maturity fund matched to the date | Credit risk funds for essential goals |
| Goal 5+ years away, wants stability | Target maturity fund, gilt or long duration (accepting rate swings), PPF | Treating debt as the whole plan; consider some equity too |
| Retiree needing regular income | SWP from a conservative debt fund; government small-savings schemes for eligible seniors; bond ladder | High-yield bonds for essential income |
| Large long-term capital gain from property | 54EC bonds (if eligible) | — |
| Wants higher yield, understands the risk | Small slice in credit risk fund or rated corporate bonds, diversified | Putting a large share in one issuer |

> **Talk-track:** “Let's decide two things before choosing a fund: when do you need this money, and how would you feel if it fell 3% in a month?”
example: Goal 1–3 years away: short duration or a target maturity fund matched to the date — not a credit risk fund for an essential goal.
say: Duration matches the goal date; credit quality matches how essential the money is.
For essential income, avoid high-yield bonds.
never: Long duration fits money needed any day.
A large share in one issuer is fine if the yield is high.

talk_track.title: Two deciding questions
talk_track.text: Let's decide two things before choosing a fund: when do you need this money, and how would you feel if it fell 3% in a month?

check.q: For money a client may need any day, the usual choice is:
check.why: Liquid or overnight fund. Lowest rate and credit risk, high liquidity.

check.q: For a goal 1–3 years away, a suitable category is:
check.why: Short duration. Duration matched to the goal.

check.q: For a goal 2 years away, which duration fits best?
o: Short duration, matched to the goal date
Any duration, if the yield is high
Duration does not matter for debt
check.why: Choose short duration to match the goal date.
